A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable 16-page ChartCoder paper, including Appendices A.1–A.5. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content.

before.justification: v2 reports original ChartCoder benchmark results in Table 3, ablation experiments in Tables 6 and 8, and additional empirical analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark results, ablation experiments, and empirical analyses, including those in the appendices.

M1.justification: The architecture, Any Resolution processing, two-stage training, and Snippet-of-Thought procedure in Sections 3–4 are identical.

E1.justification: Both use the same training datasets and evaluate the same ChartMimic, Plot2Code, ChartX, and MMC tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout the benchmark tables and supplementary experiments, including the backbone comparisons in Tables 6 and 8.

E3.justification: The zero-shot evaluations, benchmark subsets, metrics, and training settings are unchanged. Both already apply the revised Plot2Code Rating calculation described in Section 5.1.

E4.justification: Both retain identical backbone, visual-encoder, and SoT ablations, code-assisted chart understanding experiments, readability and error analyses, and case studies.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 9 retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match, including appendix results. For example, Table 3 reports identical ChartCoder ChartMimic execution, low-level, and high-level scores of 91.4, 77.4, and 74.0.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, or derivations change. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about ChartCoder, Chart2Code-160k, SoT, and performance relative to existing open-source models.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning code backbones, resolution, OCR, and code-assisted understanding are unchanged. The model-scale and broader-applicability limitations also match.

D1.justification: The code-access link, Appendix A.1 implementation details, hardware and training times, and evaluation prompts in Figures 7–8 are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, reference entries, and statements positioning the work relative to earlier research are identical.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v2 dated 27 May 2025 to v3 dated 2 July 2025. The paper's wording, headings, authors, and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, Tables 1–10, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–16 match exactly; first-page visual differences are confined to the version/date stamp.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, empirical evidence, presentation, and appendices are unchanged. Updating the arXiv stamp, adding its version hyperlink, and changing PDF metadata do not meaningfully affect the paper's quality.
